subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: Should OpenClaw support Anthropic native server tools as a provider-owned opt-in feature, and what security and replay defaults should govern web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, and allowed_callers?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it adds provider-specific config and API behavior, changes where user data and tool calls execute, and may allow provider-hosted code to call OpenClaw tools.

options.title: Design default-off provider server tools
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design covering config, native tool injection, server-block replay, docs, tests, live proof, and security defaults before implementation.

options.title: Land only narrow web search
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49949 for Anthropic native web_search while leaving web_fetch and code_execution/PTC out of scope until separately approved.

options.title: Defer hosted code execution
options.body: Allow lower-risk web_search or web_fetch exploration but require a separate security decision before any allowed_callers or provider-hosted code execution support.

recommendation.title: Design default-off provider server tools
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a staged Anthropic plugin/transport design covering config, native tool injection, server-block replay, docs, tests, live proof, and security defaults before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest current issue-discussion, blame, and recent Anthropic transport/config history signal for this product/security choice.
